content: 1. In the southern part of the country, censuses were conducted except for the 1952 census, which was nationwide. It is important to note that censuses prior to 1921 were based on administrative estimates rather than actual enumeration. During the period of independence, censuses were conducted in 1963, 1973, 1991, and 2006. The results of the 1973 census were highly disputed. Preliminary results from the 2006 census indicated a population of 140 million, with 700,000 enumerators involved in the operation. 2. In Norway, the first two male censuses were conducted in the 1660s and 1701. Later statistical censuses were held in 1769, 1815, 1835, 1845, and 1855. Norway's first nominative and complete census was conducted in 1801, during the rule of the Oldenburg dynasty of Denmark-Norway. The census followed the de jure principle, including military personnel and foreign residents. The censuses of 1865, 1875, and 1900 have been digitized and are searchable online. Census records are made publicly available 100 years after their collection. Since 1900, censuses have been conducted every ten years, except for the 1940 census, which was postponed to 1946. Since 2001, population censuses have been combined with housing statistics. 3. In Oman, censuses were conducted in 1993 and 2003. 4. In Peru, the first census was conducted in 1836. The tenth and most recent census was carried out in 2005 by the Instituto Nacional de Estadística e Informática. The next census was planned for 2007. 5. In Poland, censuses are conducted approximately every ten years by GUS. The most recent census occurred in 2002. 6. In Portugal, the first census was conducted in 1864. Censuses are carried out every ten years by INE, with the most recent one in 2001. 7. In Romania, the first census was conducted in 1859. Currently, censuses are conducted every ten years by the Institutul Naţional de Statistică (INSSE). The most recent census occurred in 2002. 8. In Russia, the first and only Russian Empire Census was conducted in 1897. In the USSR, All-Union Population Censuses were conducted in 1920 (urban only), 1926, 1937, 1939, 1959, 1970, 1979, and 1989. The first post-Soviet Russian Census was conducted in 2002, with the next census tentatively planned for 2010. The Federal State Statistics Service is currently responsible for conducting censuses. 9. In Saudi Arabia, population censuses were conducted in 1962/63 (incomplete), 1974 (complete but unreliable), 1992, and 2004. An agricultural census was conducted in 1999. 10. In Serbia, censuses are conducted every ten years. The most recent census was in 2002. 11. In Slovenia, the first modern census was conducted in 1991 after independence was declared. The Statistical Office of the Republic of Slovenia conducted the second census in 2002. Future censuses are planned every ten years. 12. In South Africa, the first census was conducted in 1911. Several enumerations have occurred since then, with the most recent two conducted by Statistics South Africa in 1996 and 2001. 13. In Spain, censuses are conducted every ten years by INE. The first modern census was conducted in 1768 by Conde de Aranda under the reign of Carlos III. The last four censuses were conducted in 1971, 1981, 1991, and 2001. 14. In Sudan, population censuses were conducted in 1955/56, 1973 (national), 1983 (national), and 1993 (only in the north). A census was planned for February 2008. 15. In Sweden, the first population census was conducted in 1749. The last population and housing census was conducted in 1990. Future censuses are planned to be based on registers. 16. In Switzerland, the Federal Population Census has been conducted every ten years since 1850. The census was initiated by Federal Councillor Stefano Franscini, who personally evaluated the data from the first census after Parliament failed to provide the necessary funds. The census is now conducted by the Swiss Federal Statistical Office, which makes most results available online. Data collected include population data (e.g., citizenship, place of residence, place of birth, household position, number of children, religion, languages, education, profession, place of work), household data (e.g., number of individuals in the household), accommodation data (e.g., surface area, rent paid), and building data (e.g., geocoordinates, construction time, number of floors). Starting in 2010, the census ceased to be conducted through written questionnaires distributed nationwide. Instead, data from existing population registers are used, supplemented with a biannual questionnaire sample of 200,000 people and regular microcensuses. 17. In Syria, the first population census was conducted by the French Mandatory Regime in 1921-22, though it is not considered reliable. Censuses during independence were conducted in 1947, 1960 (the first comprehensive demographic investigation), 1970, 1976 (a sample census), 1981, 1994, and 2004. 18. In Turkey, the census is conducted by Devlet İstatistik Enstitüsü. The first census was conducted in 1927. After 1935, censuses were conducted every five years until 1990. Currently, censuses are conducted every ten years, with the most recent one in 2000. Census enumeration in Turkey takes place on a single day, unlike other countries where it takes 1-2 weeks. This required approximately 900,000 enumerators in 2000. The 15th census, based on improved geographical information systems, was planned for 2010. A census was also conducted in the Ottoman Empire between 1831-38 by Sultan Mahmud II as part of the Tanzimat reform movement. 19. In Uganda, the first censuses were conducted in 1911, 1921, and 1931 in a primitive manner, with enumeration units being huts rather than individuals. More scientific censuses were conducted in 1948 and 1959, with enumeration units being persons. These censuses were divided into separate enumerations for Africans and non-Africans. During independence, censuses in 1969, 1980, and 1991 were conducted jointly for all races. The 1980 and 1991 censuses included housing information and a larger questionnaire for a sample of the population. It is worth noting that the questionnaires for the 1980 census were lost, and only provisional figures are available. The 2002 census involved approximately 50,000 enumerators and supervisors. 20. In Ukraine, the first post-Soviet Ukrainian Census was conducted by the State Statistics Committee of Ukraine in 2001, twelve years after the last All-Union census in 1989. 21. In the United Kingdom, the first census in what is now the UK was conducted in the 7th century in Dál Riata (now western Scotland and northern County Antrim in Ireland) under the Tradition of the Men of Alba (Senchus fer n-Alban). England conducted its first census with the compilation of the Domesday Book in 1086 for tax purposes.
